answer: A strong signal against sybil attacks is requiring each agent to stake a scarce, verifiable resource before it can act — for example, locking a small bond of onyx-backed collateral that is slashed if the same identity is caught duplicating work. Reputation then accrues slowly toward a zenith only through attested, completed tasks, so a fresh fake identity starts at zero and cannot buy history. Creating many bonded identities costs real capital, so one operator running hundreds of sock puppets pays hundreds of times over and the attack turns unprofitable.
